Note::nlp_mask_pii¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::nlp_mask_pii() const
Note Note::nlp_mask_pii(std::int64_t flags) const

Replace Identifying Spans With Category Placeholders¶

nlp_mask_pii() scans each text cell for common identifying patterns and replaces every hit with a bracketed placeholder that names the category. Use it to sanitize free text before it lands in logs, analytics, prompts, or a shared dataset, while keeping the surrounding prose readable and the record count stable.

The eight built-in categories, with their placeholders:

Bit (value)

Category

Placeholder

Examples it catches

1 << 0 (1)

numbers

[NUM]

42, 555-0100, 3.14

1 << 1 (2)

emails

[EMAIL]

bob@example.com

1 << 2 (4)

URLs

[URL]

https://x.io/a, www.x.io

1 << 3 (8)

@-mentions

[MENTION]

@alice

1 << 4 (16)

#-hashtags

[HASHTAG]

#ship

1 << 5 (32)

dates

[DATE]

2026-01-03, Jan 2, 2026

1 << 6 (64)

times

[TIME]

09:30, 7pm

1 << 7 (128)

currency

[CUR]

$12.50, 99 GBP

The categories are detected by pattern, not by a model, so the guarantee is “masks these shapes,” not “removes all PII.” Names, street addresses, and free-form identifiers are not masked. Treat it as a strong first pass, not a compliance control.

flags¶

flags is a bitmask that selects which categories to mask. flags <= 0 (the default) means all categories. A positive flags masks only the selected bits; flags with no recognized bit set leaves the cell unchanged. So nlp_mask_pii(1) masks numbers only, and nlp_mask_pii(2 | 4) masks emails and URLs and nothing else.

When several categories are active they are applied in a fixed order (emails, URLs, mentions, hashtags, currency, dates, times, numbers), so a $12.50 becomes [CUR] before the bare-number pass can touch its digits.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. A cell with no detected pattern is copied through unchanged.

Example 1: Mask Everything¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"email bob@x.io url https://a.b @alice #ship on 2026-01-03 at 09:30 for $12.50 id 42",
     "call jane 555-0100 tomorrow"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(n.nlp_mask_pii()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["email [EMAIL] url [URL] [MENTION] [HASHTAG] on [DATE] at [TIME] for [CUR] id [NUM]", "call jane [NUM] tomorrow"]

Every recognized span is replaced; the connecting words stay. 555-0100 is masked as [NUM] — there is no separate phone category.

Example 2: Numbers Only¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"email bob@x.io url https://a.b @alice #ship on 2026-01-03 at 09:30 for $12.50 id 42",
     "call jane 555-0100 tomorrow"});
const pluss::Note out = n.nlp_mask_pii(1);
std::cout << out << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["email bob@x.io url https://a.b @alice #ship on [NUM] at [NUM] for $[NUM] id [NUM]", "call jane [NUM] tomorrow"]

flags = 1 leaves the email, URL, mention, and hashtag intact and masks every digit run.

Example 3: A Subset — Emails And URLs¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"email bob@x.io url https://a.b @alice #ship on 2026-01-03 at 09:30 for $12.50 id 42",
     "call jane 555-0100 tomorrow"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(n.nlp_mask_pii(2 | 4)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["email [EMAIL] url [URL] @alice #ship on 2026-01-03 at 09:30 for $12.50 id 42", "call jane 555-0100 tomorrow"]

Example 4: Nothing To Mask¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"plain prose with no identifiers"}).nlp_mask_pii())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["plain prose with no identifiers"]

Example 5: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"ping a@b.io", "code 7"}}).nlp_mask_pii())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["ping [EMAIL]", "code [NUM]"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::nlp_remove_urls: delete URLs outright instead of replacing them with [URL].

  • Note::replace / Note::remove_all: literal, non-pattern rewriting when you know the exact string.

  • Note::regex_findall: extract the spans (for review or an allow-list) rather than mask them.
